sources.support: Fortune reports that Nike identified itself through a victim-impact statement filed before Christina Chapman's sentencing. The report says Nike described hiring an unnamed worker in Chapman's network for five months, paying about $75,000, and spending time and resources on an internal investigation. Normalized boundary: Fortune reports that Nike publicly identified itself in a victim-impact filing as having hired an unnamed worker in the Chapman network. Attribution boundary: Secondary report of a first-party court filing. Nike did not comment to Fortune, and the underlying victim-impact statement was not recovered in the cited evidence. Publication boundary: Hold pending direct recovery of the public filing. Do not use this report to reverse-map Nike to any anonymized Company number in indictments or to identify the unnamed worker
